title: The fork
line: One piece attacks two at once. The knight does it best.

steps.text: A fork is one piece attacking two at once. Here the knight on c7 attacks the king and the rook. Only one can be saved.
Find the same fork here: one knight move that attacks the king and the rook on a8.

wrong.d5e7: That takes a pawn, but the bishop on f8 takes the knight back.

steps.hint: The knight lands on a square your bishop also guards.
steps.after: Check, and the rook on a8 is attacked too.

steps.text: The king had to move. Take the rook.
A fork with check is the strongest kind. Tap the square where your knight would check the king and attack the queen.

wrong.d6: From there the knight attacks neither the king nor the queen.
wrong.g5: From there the knight attacks neither the king nor the queen.
wrong.c5: From there the knight attacks the queen, but not the king.

steps.after: From there the knight attacks the king and the queen.
Black must answer the check, and the queen is left to the knight.
A queen for nothing. The king had to answer the check first.

summary: A fork attacks two pieces at once, and only one can be saved. Look for squares where one piece hits two.
